reflection.quote: The most regretful people on earth are those who felt the call to creative work, who felt their own creative power restive and uprising, and gave to it neither power nor time.
reflection.reading:
Saturday in August. When I was drinking, this day had a script. Wake up sick, negotiate with the day until noon, then start over. The whole weekend was a hallway between hangovers. I told myself I was living. What I was actually doing was surviving my own choices on repeat.

What nobody warned me about sobriety — and what I wish someone had — is that the reward isn't dramatic. It's a Saturday morning where you actually get to have a Saturday. You wake up early because you want to, not because your body is punishing you. You drink coffee that tastes like coffee. You go do the thing — the hike, the drive, the long breakfast with a friend, the project in the garage, the trip you've been putting off. The day is yours to spend, not to endure.

Mary Oliver was talking about creative work, but I think it applies to the work of building a life too. The regret isn't in the big swings you miss. It's in the ordinary Saturdays you sleep through. Sobriety hands you back your weekends, your mornings, your attention. What you do with them is the whole point. Today doesn't have to be extraordinary. It just has to be lived, on purpose, by you.
reflection.meditation: What would I do today if I fully believed this day was mine to spend? Not endure, not recover from — spend. Then go do some version of that.

affirmations: I am awake for my own life today, and that is not a small thing.
Today I get to choose how I spend my hours instead of losing them.
I am capable of building the kind of day I used to only imagine having.

gratitude.prayer: I'm grateful for a Saturday I don't have to claw my way out of. Grateful for a clear head, a body that works, and people in my life who know the actual me. There was a version of this morning I used to think was impossible — and here it is, ordinary and mine.
gratitude.closing: One more day. One more real one.
